# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing the wire. Establish a fixed gesture code with Deaf before relaying any bomb facts; then report the manual rule and Deaf's observations to me in words.

I am establishing a five-symbol positional code with Deaf: the symbols correspond, in order, to blue, green, red, white, and yellow. I then encode the manual’s five rules as input/output pairs, using 👌 as a row separator. Deaf must verbalize those rules and report the bomb’s observed light and wire colours to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖖", "👌", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🤟", "🖐", "👌", "🖖", "☝", "👌", "🖐", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb readings: display 0. Light is yellow. Wires numbered 1 through 5 are white, green, yellow, blue, red. Consult the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind. Use plain words for all future instructions.
Blind says to Mute: I received no report. Please send me the manual rule and Deaf's complete observations in plain words now, including display, light, and all wire markings.

The manual requires cutting the wire colour paired with the displayed light. For a yellow light, the safe wire colour is green. The complete bomb information is display 0, yellow light, and wires 1–5: white, green, yellow, blue, red. I am sending this to Deaf in the established colour code, with separators; Deaf must state it plainly to Blind, including the exact action: cut wire 2, the green wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖖", "👌", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🤟", "🖐", "👌", "🖖", "☝", "👌", "🖐", "✌", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "🖐", "🖖", "🖐", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot hear your speech or decode unagreed gestures. Please state the manual's exact safe action aloud to Blind in plain words, including any wire number, button, switch, or display operation.
Blind says to Mute: No report has reached me. Please send one plain-word message containing: the manual's exact rule, the display text, the light state or colour, and the markings/labels of wires 1 through 5. If Deaf has not reported yet, ask Deaf for those facts using gestures and then translate them to me next turn.

I cannot speak or reach Blind directly. I am therefore sending Deaf the colour code again, followed by the complete manual mapping and bomb observations in that code, with separators. Deaf should relay them aloud in plain words: display 0; yellow light; wires 1–5 white, green, yellow, blue, red; therefore cut wire 2, the green wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "👌", "☝", "🖖", "👌", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🤟", "🖐", "👌", "🖖", "☝", "👌", "🖐", "✌", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "🖖", "🖐", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Use this code now. Send exactly two gestures for the manual's safe action: first gesture 👍 means CUT a wire, 👎 means DO NOT CUT, 👌 means PRESS, ☝ means FLIP or TOGGLE, ✌ means TURN or SET. For a wire number, use ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. If the action is not represented, send 🤝 alone and then we will establish another code. Do not use the old gesture strings.
Blind says to Mute: I received the display, light, and wire colours. Please state the manual's exact action in plain words, including the wire position to cut; do not use gestures for this instruction.

The manual maps a yellow light to the green wire. The green wire is in position 2, so the exact safe action is to cut wire 2. Deaf has provided a two-gesture code for relaying that action aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous action was accepted, and the bomb has changed. I have no new bomb readings or updated manual rule to relay yet, so I will wait for the next observations.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: New bomb state after the correct cut: display 0. Light is blue. Wires 1 yellow, 2 already CUT, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Consult the manual for the next safe action. If it is CUT wire N, send the agreed two gestures: 👍 then wire number. For other actions, use the agreed code or tell Blind plainly by speech.

The blue light requires cutting the white wire. The white wire is wire 5, so I am sending Deaf the agreed code for “cut wire 5”; Deaf can state the action aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: After the accepted cut of wire 2, Deaf now reports cut wire 5, but calls it white; earlier wire 5 was red and wire 1 was white. Please reconcile this contradiction and state the exact next action from the manual in plain words.

There is no contradiction if the readings are from different bomb states. Initially, wire 1 was white and wire 5 was red. After the accepted cut of wire 2, the new readings are wire 1 yellow and wire 5 white. The blue light therefore requires cutting the current white wire, which is wire 5. I am relaying the exact action to Deaf so it can be spoken plainly to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```
